issue.title: [Bug] ChatGPT API active account reads Codex quota via loginQuota; missing SIWC quota card (v0.1.1567)
issue.body:
## Summary

The built-in **ChatGPT API** provider (`chatgpt-api`, Sign in with ChatGPT / SIWC) incorrectly displays the **currently active Codex account's** 5-hour and 7-day usage windows under the ChatGPT API account. The normal CLI quota report / Usage panel, meanwhile, does not include a `chatgpt-api` subscription card.

This is **not evidence that SIWC has a separately queryable quota**: the observed percentages come through Codex's `/wham/usage` path and Codex credentials, not the SIWC authorization. The cross-provider misattribution may also feed account-allowance routing and persisted cache/history.

**Affected version:** `magpie 0.1.1567`, verified against source tag [v0.1.1567](https://github.com/yetone/magpie/tree/v0.1.1567).

## Reproduction / observed behavior

1. Have a Codex ChatGPT subscription login and a separate `ChatGPT API` (SIWC) provider login enabled in Magpie; both are marked `active: true` in their respective provider account lists.
2. Open the provider editors: ChatGPT API incorrectly shows 5h / 7d allowance meters resembling Codex's.
3. Run `magpie accounts --json` and compare the **sanitized** `codex` and `chatgpt-api` entries. Observed:

| Agent | 5 hours used | 5 hours resetsAt | 7 days used | 7 days resetsAt |
| --- | ---: | --- | ---: | --- |
| `codex` | 50% | `2026-10-26T19:27:52+08:00` | 8% | `2026-11-02T14:27:52+08:00` |
| `chatgpt-api` | 50% | `2026-10-26T19:27:52+08:00` | 8% | `2026-11-02T14:27:52+08:00` |

Both entries reported `active: true`, `plan: plus`, and no error.

4. Run `magpie quota --json`. Only the `codex` entry is present. At the later read Codex 5h usage was 51%, with the *same* 5h / 7d reset timestamps; there was still no `chatgpt-api` entry.

The identical percent and reset timestamps, together with the code path below, indicate that the SIWC account's displayed windows originate from Codex, **not from an SIWC usage endpoint**. Account email addresses and tokens are intentionally omitted.

## Source-level root cause (tag v0.1.1567)

1. [`internal/provider/side_logins.go`](https://github.com/yetone/magpie/blob/v0.1.1567/internal/provider/side_logins.go#L117-L153): `listSideLogins` marks the first SIWC saved login as `Active = true`. Here `Active` simply means the first account in that provider's own list.
2. [`internal/provider/login_usage.go`](https://github.com/yetone/magpie/blob/v0.1.1567/internal/provider/login_usage.go#L286-L370): `builtinLogins` supports `ChatGPTAPIID`, but `loginQuota` has no `ChatGPTAPIID` branch. Its generic `case l.Active:` calls `codexToken(ctx, codexHome())`, followed by `codexWindowsRenewing(...)` for any active provider account that reaches this switch—not just Codex. The returned `SubscriptionQuota.Provider` remains `chatgpt-api`, so Codex's windows are attributed to the wrong provider/user.

```go
switch {
case l.Agent == "claude":
case l.Active: // BUG: also true for the first chatgpt-api account
    tok, accountID, err = codexToken(ctx, codexHome())
    renew = func(ctx context.Context, stale string) (string, string, error) {
        return codexTokenRenewing(ctx, codexHome(), stale)
    }
default:
    tok, accountID, err = savedLoginToken(ctx, l.Agent, l.User)
}
// For anything other than Claude, the successful path then uses codexWindowsRenewing.
```

3. A **non-active SIWC account** reaches `savedLoginToken(ctx, ChatGPTAPIID, user)` instead; [`internal/provider/logins_on.go`](https://github.com/yetone/magpie/blob/v0.1.1567/internal/provider/logins_on.go#L198-L290) only implements that saved-token path for Codex and otherwise returns an unsupported-agent error. SIWC's actual token handler is `siwcFresh` in `chatgpt_api.go`.
4. [`internal/provider/subscription_usage.go`](https://github.com/yetone/magpie/blob/v0.1.1567/internal/provider/subscription_usage.go#L398-L531) registers Codex `fetches` but not SIWC; and [`internal/provider/cards_kept.go`](https://github.com/yetone/magpie/blob/v0.1.1567/internal/provider/cards_kept.go#L29-L102) omits `ChatGPTAPIID` from `accountCard` and `cardAgents`. This explains why `magpie quota --json` / the top-level allowance panel lack SIWC.
5. **Potential downstream effects** worth testing: [`Allowances(agent)`](https://github.com/yetone/magpie/blob/v0.1.1567/internal/provider/routing.go#L500-L556) consumes `loginUsageAt(ctx, agent)`; [`keepReading`/`keepLast`](https://github.com/yetone/magpie/blob/v0.1.1567/internal/provider/quota_refresh.go#L37-L42) can persist successful misattributed readings as `chatgpt-api/<user>` in `quotas.json`, and the per-agent usage history can record them too. I have **not** independently verified a particular routing decision or persisted entry in this installation.

## SIWC usage-query availability (follow-up, 2026-10-26)

This turns out to be an **upstream capability gap as well as a Magpie provider-dispatch bug**. Please **do not fix the UI by copying a Codex account's 5h/7d readings into SIWC**, even if the two logins have the same email.

- OpenAI's published [SIWC Accounts and sessions / Tracking usage](https://developers.openai.com/siwc/token-sharing-open-source/profiles-and-sessions) documentation directs apps to **ChatGPT Settings → Usage**. It says the **Plus five-hour plan usage is shared across apps**, but this is a statement about *usage accounting*, **not** authorization to read `/backend-api/wham/usage` with a SIWC OAuth token.
- The official [SIWC UI/UX guidelines](https://developers.openai.com/siwc/ui-ux-guidelines) direct integrators to offer a **Manage usage** link, including when an app-specific limit is reached; they do not document a SIWC endpoint that returns window usage percentages/reset timestamps.
- The official [SIWC Errors and recovery](https://developers.openai.com/siwc/token-sharing-open-source/errors-and-recovery) guidance says `subscription_sharing_usage_limit_exceeded` (429) may indicate **an app-specific limit**, and **must not** be used alone to assume the overall ChatGPT plan is exhausted or to infer a reset time.
- Independently reported upstream: [openai/codex#54219 — “Sign in with ChatGPT token sharing: no way for apps to read ChatGPT plan usage”](https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/54219) (opened 2026-10-15, still open when checked). Its reporter tested a SIWC `chatgpt.tokens.use.direct` token on 2026-10-14: `GET https://chatgpt.com/backend-api/wham/usage` returned `401 rejected_by_access_enforcement / no_matching_rule`; successful `GET /v1/models` and streamed `POST /v1/responses` responses did **not** provide Codex-style `x-codex-primary-*`/`x-codex-secondary-*` rate-limit headers or a rate-limit stream event. These are *that reporter's tests*, not a claim that every conceivable undocumented endpoint has been probed.

**Implications for the fix:**

1. **Correctness/security first:** make `loginQuota` explicitly dispatch `ChatGPTAPIID` before any Codex-only handling; prevent both active and non-active SIWC logins from querying Codex credentials or `/wham/usage`. Cover the case where the active Codex login and active SIWC login belong to **different** users/workspaces.
2. **Honest quota representation:** until OpenAI exposes a **documented/authorized SIWC usage query**, show `unknown/unavailable` and link to [ChatGPT Usage](https://chatgpt.com/settings/usage). A per-request `usage.input_tokens/output_tokens` object is not a plan-quota percentage. A 429 is an error signal, not a reset clock.
3. **Avoid polluted state:** ensure a previously cached `chatgpt-api/<user>` Codex-derived reading cannot continue to affect GUI meters, `Allowances("chatgpt-api")` routing decisions, or quota history as if it were genuine SIWC usage.
4. **If offering Codex-derived *reference* data in future:** require an explicit, verified account/workspace match and label it clearly as a *shared-plan reference* (not SIWC app-specific availability); don't treat it as a reliable SIWC routing quota. This is optional and **not** a prerequisite for the bug fix.
5. A future true SIWC quota reader can be added only after a supported source with well-defined identity, scopes, quota windows, and reset semantics becomes available.

## Expected behavior

- A `chatgpt-api` login must **never** query the Codex account token or blindly reuse Codex's `/wham/usage` windows on the basis of `l.Active`.
- SIWC accounts should use an explicitly supported SIWC usage-reading path, if one exists; otherwise report **allowance unavailable/unknown**, with a pointer to ChatGPT's Usage page, and not present made-up or misattributed 5h/7d percentages.
- The normal quota panel and `magpie quota --json` should represent SIWC accounts consistently, at minimum with an honest unavailable state.
- Routing should treat an unknown SIWC quota as unknown, not as Codex quota. Stale wrong SIWC readings should not survive the fix as valid usage readings.

## Suggested fix / regression coverage

- Add an explicit `ChatGPTAPIID` branch before the Codex token switch in `loginQuota` (return a known-unavailable `SubscriptionQuota` until a valid SIWC allowance API is available).
- Restrict `case l.Active:` to `l.Agent == "codex" && l.Active`, and avoid a Codex-specific fallback for other agents.
- Register an SIWC account card (`accountCard`, `cardAgents`, `fetchSubscriptionUsage`) with clear unavailable/unknown status; don't simply copy Codex windows into SIWC.
- Add tests for first/active SIWC account (no `codexToken` or `/wham/usage` call), secondary/non-active SIWC account (no Codex saved-token path), different Codex and SIWC login identities, absence/presence in CLI quota reports, and previously persisted `chatgpt-api` false windows.

**Scope note:** `siwcProvider` already signs actual inference requests with SIWC's own `siwcFresh` token. This report is specifically about **allowance-reading/account attribution**; it does not claim that SIWC model inference uses Codex credentials.

comments.body:
Fixed on a fork branch: `fix/3721-siwc-quota` (head `20ac3a6c`, on upstream `6afbe3f3`) — a ChatGPT-API login is no longer read as a Codex account.

**Root cause.** `internal/provider/login_usage.go`'s `loginQuota` had `case l.Active: tok, accountID, err = codexToken(ctx, codexHome())` — and `internal/provider/side_logins.go` marks the first account of *every* side login `Active`, so a ChatGPT-API (SIWC) login fell into the Codex branch and reported Codex's windows or "Codex is signed out".

**Change.** the Codex branch is guarded by the agent id (`l.Agent == "codex" && l.Active`), and a SIWC login returns an explicit `Error` naming its own usage URL instead of borrowing Codex's windows. The missing SIWC quota card is a separate call and is not added here.

**Verified.** Red: `go test -tags nogui ./internal/provider/ -run TestChatGPTAPIQuotaIsNotCodex` → `chatgpt_api_test.go:366: me@example.com (active true): "Codex is signed out; run codex login"` (the second account said `chatgpt-api accounts can't be used side by side`)
Green: `same command → `ok`; the package's 1004 tests pass, only `TestUnreadLoginsWriteErrorsKeepCredentials` fails and it fails on unmodified base too (synctest)` → `ok github.com/yetone/magpie/internal/provider`

Not verified: a real SIWC account. The error text is shown as an error, not as an allowance — `Count` prints nothing for it.

Full `go test -tags nogui ./...` over round 26's branches: 70 packages ok, 5 red (edit `TestWriteAtomicReadOnlyHardLink`, gateway's five, plugin `TestPluginSOCKSProxy`, provider's synctest fatal in `TestUnreadLoginsWriteErrorsKeepCredentials`, testenv `TestProgram`) — every one of them reproduces identically at base `6afbe3f3` in this environment (umask 0027), so none is from this change.

Branch: https://github.com/skygunner/magpie/tree/fix/3721-siwc-quota — no PR opened, this repo takes no external PRs; say the word if you'd rather have the patch inline here.

issue.title: ChatGPT API provider cannot select an OpenAI Organization or API credits organization

repository.name: magpie
repository.description: Every agent's model. One place. Codex on DeepSeek, Claude Code on Kimi, from the menu bar.

issue.body:
## Problem

The built-in `ChatGPT API` provider (Sign in with ChatGPT / SIWC) does not provide a way to select the OpenAI API Organization that should receive requests.

This matters for ChatGPT subscriptions that have an API credits grant attached to a specific API Organization. After signing in to ChatGPT, Magpie uses the account's OAuth token, but there is no organization selector, Organization ID setting, or `OpenAI-Organization` request header. Users cannot tell Magpie to use a different eligible API Organization.

## Source-level observation

In `internal/provider/chatgpt_api.go`:

- `siwcAPI` is fixed to `https://api.openai.com/v1`.
- `siwcCreds` stores the OAuth client, account, token, scopes, and expiry, but no organization or project ID.
- `siwcProvider` signs requests with only `Authorization: Bearer <token>` (plus session headers).
- The OAuth flow requests the `chatgpt.tokens.use.direct` scope, so this is the ChatGPT subscription-sharing provider rather than a normal API-key provider.

Relevant code:

- https://github.com/yetone/magpie/blob/main/internal/provider/chatgpt_api.go#L3-L17
- https://github.com/yetone/magpie/blob/main/internal/provider/chatgpt_api.go#L79-L90
- https://github.com/yetone/magpie/blob/main/internal/provider/chatgpt_api.go#L717-L743

## Expected behavior

Please consider one of these options:

1. Add an Organization ID / Project ID field to the ChatGPT API provider, if the SIWC API supports selecting them.
2. Expose a standard OpenAI API-key provider with Organization / Project configuration so users can explicitly target the API Organization containing their credits.
3. If SIWC tokens cannot select an Organization by design, show that clearly in the UI and document that this provider uses ChatGPT plan usage rather than API Organization credits.

The related #3721 issue about SIWC quota attribution appears relevant: it also shows that the ChatGPT API provider and Codex provider currently have different, partially unsupported usage/account semantics.
